our work provides a new and promising approach for the quantitative analysis of microfluidic flows.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for measuring interfacial tension in microfluidic devices, by deforming droplets through a constriction and fitting our model with the experimental results.
we have developed a method to measure interfacial tensions in a microfluidic flow-focusing device, which can be applied to any droplet system.

we have demonstrated that a numerical model of the flow in the microfluidic chip, combined with a model of the droplet deformation and a fitting procedure, can be used to measure the interfacial tensions of droplets in microfluidic chips with an accuracy of a few percent.

, in order to perform a proper rheological analysis, one must be able to quantify the stress exerted by the flow on the sample.
the stress applied on a droplet by the flow-focusing device can be calculated with a good accuracy, which enables the measurement of the droplet interfacial tension.
